simplesect.para: The APFloat must be built using semantics, that can be represented by the host double type without loss of precision. It can be IEEEdouble and shorter semantics, like IEEEsingle and others.

briefdescription.para: Converts this APFloat to host float value.

simplesect.para: The APFloat must be built using semantics, that can be represented by the host float type without loss of precision. It can be IEEEquad and shorter semantics, like IEEEdouble and others. Converts this APFloat to host float value.
The APFloat must be built using semantics, that can be represented by the host float type without loss of precision. It can be IEEEsingle and shorter semantics, like IEEEhalf.

briefdescription.para: We don't rely on operator== working on double values, as it returns true for things that are clearly not equal, like -0.0 and 0.0.

detaileddescription.para: As such, this method can be used to do an exact bit-for-bit comparison of two floating point values.
We leave the version with the double argument here because it's just so convenient to write "2.0" and the like. Without this function we'd have to duplicate its logic everywhere it's called.
